DEVELOPER INSIGHTS

Early Contractor Involvement Below Ground: Make the Workshop Produce Decisions

Use specialist input to resolve specific uncertainties before procurement hardens.

In this insight

Choose the questions worth answeringKeep advice and commitment distinctBring the right disciplines togetherTranslate learning into the tenderFor your project discussionDiscuss a project ↗

Educational overview · Project-specific design and execution require qualified review.

Choose the questions worth answering

Early involvement is useful when it addresses a defined decision: access feasibility, package boundaries, sequence options or missing information. Set an agenda around those questions. A general presentation of company capability may be informative, but it is not the same as a working session that improves the project brief. Provide the information needed for participants to prepare.

Keep advice and commitment distinct

At an early stage, some suggestions will depend on further investigation or design. Record those conditions. Do not treat a workshop comment as a priced commitment or approved solution. Ask for a concise output that distinguishes observations, options, assumptions and recommended next actions. This preserves the value of the discussion without overstating its certainty.

Bring the right disciplines together

Include the people who understand the design, procurement, construction sequence and site constraints. The specialist can identify practical issues, but other parties may control the decisions needed to resolve them. Assign owners during the workshop. A cross-disciplinary discussion is most effective when it ends with a route to closing the identified interfaces.

Translate learning into the tender

Update the scope, information pack and programme assumptions using the accepted outputs. Keep a record of why decisions were made and what remains open. Where procurement rules require equal information to bidders, manage that through the appropriate process. The commercial benefit of early involvement comes from a better-defined project, not merely from holding an additional meeting before tender.

For your project discussion

Use these questions to structure a conversation with the project’s qualified design and delivery team. This article is general procurement guidance, not a site-specific design, method statement or compliance assessment. The cited international resources provide background; applicable local requirements and the approved project documents govern the work.

Take this into your next conversation

  • Focus the workshop on specific decisions.
  • Label provisional advice and assumptions.
  • Carry accepted outcomes into procurement documents.

References & further reading

  • Further reading: FHWA — Geotechnical technical guidance

International references provide technical context; applicable local requirements and the project engineer’s decisions govern the actual works.
